body:
Please provide direct feedback about what you would like to see changed. In other words, explain what in particular is broken in the new theme and what you expect it to look like instead. 

This is a space to report _bugs_ not a place to complain in general. So please keep your bug reports actionable and to the point.

@clayjohn Apologies, I've added examples of changes that this has introduced as examples of issues. These link to issues that were raised in the PR a month ago that were left unchanged when the PR was merged a month later. I have also created this ticket on the insistence of @coppolaemilio who had recommended creating an Issue regarding this PR merge.

Additionally, my example for what it should look like is the Classic Godot Theme. This can be viewed by opening Godot 4.5 Stable.

I've also changed the "Proposed Resolution" section to read "Proposed Resolution/Action" to address "So please keep your bug reports actionable", reverting this PR will address the issues I am raising.

leaving the style preset at classic with old (or close enough) base color for now would also be preferable imo if people are really intent on continuing cooking the new theme in-tree. at the very least put some of the background fills back in, the theme contrast option is largely ruined without them

Agreed with @shakesoda, I would not have as much of an issue with adding this theme if it wasn't set as the new Default Theme. Making a theme the default option is radically different from adding it as another option, and there should be more consensus before setting a new, incomplete theme as the default theme.

Just a reminder, this isn't a general complaints thread. We want specific actionable feedback. 

Describe precisely what you consider to be a bug. Explain why it's a bug and articulate what you think the behaviour should be. 

Just simply saying you don't like it and want to go back to the old theme will result in nothing happening. The old theme is still an option in the editor settings. If you want to help improve the new theme, then be constructive

Hi @clayjohn ,

I updated the description to have the specific examples that you requested in [this comment](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/112229#issuecomment-3470830289). You can find them in the section "Specific Issues with New Theme". This was added shortly before I made [this comment](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/112229#issuecomment-3470868463), so I can understand the new information being missed.

@clayjohn ,

I have updated the section "Proposed Resolution/Action" to now contain two action points. I agree with another suggestion that adding this new theme as an additional theme and not the default would be acceptable, at least until the new theme no longer has issues with the layout as described in the section "Specific Issues with New Theme".

@clayjohn I'm sorry, I linked to several examples of this new theme being incomplete and affecting usability while being a default theme. These issues were also brought up and unaddressed in the PR. @coppolaemilio said to raise an issue, so I am. How is this not what @coppolaemilio was asking for?

Additonally, you've hidden [this comment](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/112229#issuecomment-3470958578) for being off-topic, but it has a reasonable request to not set this theme as default until the bugs and other issues are worked out. Is that unreasonable?

Also regarding "you can see from the original PR that 10x as many people prefer the new theme than people who dislike it", there is still no answer on how this theme was selected as a new default theme. Was there a GitHub proposal ticket that requested a new theme and selected this one?

Alright, you are getting fully off topic now. 

> How is this not what coppolaemilio was asking for?

Because you haven't made a proper issue. You have just opened a ticket and used it as a space to vent your complaints. As it is, this falls far below the standard for what we expect in a proper bug report. 

> Additonally, you've hidden https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/112229#issuecomment-3470958578 for being off-topic, but it has a reasonable request to not set this theme as default until the bugs and other issues are worked out. Is that unreasonable?

Yes, it is unreasonable. And off topic

> Also regarding "you can see from the original PR that 10x as many people prefer the new theme than people who dislike it", there is still no answer on how this theme was selected as a new default theme. Was there a GitHub proposal ticket that requested a new theme and selected this one?

This new theme has been highly requested by the community for the last year and was discussed heavily by the core Godot contributors (who ultimately get the final say on all changes to the engine) and agreed to go forward. 

Again, you are getting off topic. This is your last warning. Stop complaining about the process and demanding the PR be reverted. Provide actionable feedback with a suggestion for what changes you would like to see. If you can't do that, then I am going to unsubscribe from this thread and you will be completely ignored. 

Here is an example of an actionable bug report that relates to the new theme https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/112232 This sort of report gives us the feedback we need to actually improve the new theme. Please edit your report to be like this example
@clayjohn The new theme uses similar or identical colors on some UI components, causing some container boundaries to blend together and lack distinction.

One thing I don't like about the new theme is that the click targets feel unbalanced. Tabs are now almost twice as big (vertically) than nodes, for example. So the editor feels a bit unpleasant to navigate now, some elements are harder to click. | || |---|---| --- The inspector elements also feel unbalanced. There is no good reason (?) for group titles to be as big as buttons and tabs. They basically look like buttons now 🤔 (I don't know what these elements are called, I'm talking about **Node3D** and **Node** labels) | || |---|---|
I suggest my edit with slightly more depth

Properties are now different heights and I really don't like how it looks (look at how uneven the text is). Integer and float properties are smaller in height (26px on my editor scale), while dropdowns, booleans, arrays and resources are bigger (31px). The array button also sticks out way too much imo.

> I suggest my edit with slightly more depth

I opened a similar proposal for such a change. See https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/13581

Don't know if first to notice or already fixed, but this is not improvement. This is opposite of good design. Maybe just a problem of the theme, but things should align. Now that the background is gone, they don't.

Fair enough. I just stumbled on https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/112504 which partially addresses the issue and contains some discussion on exactly what you mentioned. So it seems like there is already some awareness from people who are more knowledgeable!

adding problems I mentioned in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/112653

Classic Theme doesn't fully revert the changes.
The observed differences are with Contrast and Font not reverting (colors too but that's relatively obvious that you change Color Preset just below), with no clear documentation to fully manually revert the changes
*Suggestion moved to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/112754#issuecomment-3567822638.*
A tiny annoyance - theme panel's tabs require scrolling now: (v4.6.beta3.official [76dda5c6c]) |Classic|Modern| -|- |||
Edit button is probably bigger than it should be. (compact spacing) (v4.6.rc1.official [481f36ed2])

Glad to see that the spacing issue I brought up was addressed. >The array button also sticks out way too much imo. This is still an issue though and it goes a bit deeper, there is generally a lot of inconsistency whether or not a button is light or dark. Light buttons: - Arrays - Dictionaries - Node References and Node Paths - The button on `export_file` I feel like there should be more consistency between these (and other parts of the editor), so my suggestion would be either making all of them dark or give them a more consistent, which would mainly involve just making the resource picker light with dark buttons on the side, as well as making enums light (unless the global enums are made dark, see below). And also dropdowns everywhere else in the editor are light, and I feel like dark dropdowns would look nicer + it'd make a distinction from clickable buttons which seem to never be dark.

A couple of issues I've found. I'm using the latest master v4.6.rc.custom_build [9820f40f9] with default theme settings. Toggle buttons are hard to differentiate between toggled or not: The `Open Editor` in an animation blend tree blends with the panel bg color when selected: Same with the animation progress bar when the node is selected:
Another issue I've found. The effects panel of the buses in the `Audio` dock covers the bottom dock buttons: It also happens in the classic theme:
Bisection of the Audio dock issue points towards #114572. CC @boozee.

Roger, I can reproduce. I'll check for a possible fix asap.

I already found the problem:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/741fb8a30687d0662ab6b5c04a2a531440dd29d9/scene/gui/tree.cpp#L5117-L5119
